beats.text: The farm families around Kingsbury had to leave. It was 1940, and the Army had picked their land for a war plant.
beats.label: KINGSBURY, LAPORTE COUNTY

beats.text: More than 13,000 acres of farms became the Kingsbury Ordnance Plant.
beats.label: THE ORDNANCE PLANT
beats.credit: WKVI; The History Museum; Towne Post

beats.text: It loaded shells and ammunition for World War 2. At its peak, more than 20,000 people worked there, and nearly half were women.
beats.label: WORLD WAR 2

beats.text: A whole new town went up beside it. Today, it's Kingsford Heights.
beats.label: A WARTIME TOWN

beats.text: After the war, and a second run for Korea, the plant shut down for good. But out in the woods, rows of old ammunition bunkers still stand.
beats.label: IN THE WOODS

beats.text: Part of the old plant is an industrial park now. And part of it is the Kingsbury Fish and Wildlife Area, open to the public.
beats.label: TODAY

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
